item.title: FCC bans two devices with surveillance chips linked to Huawei
item.description: The banned items — a wireless video transmitter and dashboard camera — are made with chips manufactured by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon, which markets its products as “designed for the surveillance market.”

item.title: UK proposes 14-year prison terms for undersea cable sabotage
item.description: In an era of hybrid threats, the British government wants to update the Submarine Telegraph Act 1885, which carries a maximum fine of £1,000 and five years’ imprisonment in cases of deliberate damage.

item.title: Quest Diagnostics warns of potential data theft after attack on lab service system
item.description: Nationwide lab test company Quest Diagnostics said one of its key systems may have experienced a breach of patient data.

item.title: Reports of PHP bug exploitation attempts grow as experts downplay viability of exploits
item.description: The headline-grabbing bugs known colloquially as PHP2Shell are giving cyber analysts a lot to track — and a lot to debunk.

item.title: Toronto crime tips org freezes operations after details of data breach come to light
item.description: Late Wednesday night the Toronto chapter of Crime Stoppers broke ranks with the national association, revealing a timeline showing what it knew and when along with an announcement that it will pause operations.
